item.title: Iran War Updates: Long-Term Energy Crisis Looms as Trump Says Truce Is on ‘Life Support’
item.description: Iran defended its demands for a peace deal and President Trump called them “garbage.” Mr. Trump said he wanted to suspend the federal gasoline tax, which would require congressional approval.

item.title: Israel Says It Killed a Hezbollah Chief Near Beirut, Testing the Truce
item.description: The strike was the first near the Lebanese capital since a cease-fire that has curbed fighting but not halted it. Washington is pushing for a lasting peace, hoping it will ease diplomacy with Iran.

item.title: What to Know About the Hantavirus Outbreak on an Atlantic Cruise Ship
item.description: The health authorities are working to calm fears and contain the rare virus. Three passengers died after traveling on the ship, and several others fell ill or tested positive.

item.title: Altar Boy Who Called Out Sexual Abuse in the Philippines Is Now a Lawyer for Victims
item.description: Michal Gatchalian dared to speak out against sexual abuse by a priest in the devoutly Catholic Philippines. He’s now a lawyer helping other victims.

item.title: Former Hostage Calls on All of Israel’s Government to Resign
item.description: Rom Braslavski, who said he had endured starvation, torture and sexual abuse during two-year captivity, demanded that members “take responsibility and get out of our lives.”

item.title: Thailand’s Thaksin Shinawatra Is Out of Prison. What Will He Do Now?
item.description: Mr. Thaksin has long been a foil to Thailand’s conservative establishment. He still holds significant influence, with his political party a member of the governing coalition.

item.title: Emirates Doubles Down on U.S. and Israeli Ties Amid Iran War
item.description: The United Arab Emirates has borne the brunt of Iranian attacks throughout the war, hardening the government’s resolve to reassess its list of friends and foes.

item.title: How to Win Eurovision With Just a Few Hundred Voters
item.description: Exclusive voting data shows that, despite Eurovision’s assurances, an Israeli campaign could easily have influenced last year’s contest.

item.title: Is France’s Centrist Leader Trying to Weatherproof It From the Far Right?
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron has appointed a string of allies who will remain in critical state positions after next year’s presidential election, and who could thwart a far-right successor.

item.title: How the Fight Over Israel Is Playing Out Inside MAGA
item.description: The war in Iran has added to a tectonic shift in public opinion — a bipartisan swing away from Israel. Some on the far-right are fighting to keep President Trump’s movement aligned with the Jewish state.
